observed: All eight generated boards were inspected inline, including retained Caelith v1 and revised v2.
All seven selected boards contain two adult variants with front, profile and back views.
Plain clothing, natural beast heads and distinct species palettes are visible.

human.review_note: Grounded adult proportions and plain garments. Male facial hair and female shoulder-length hair are examples only; the four faces and four hairstyles per sex remain separate work.

goblin.review_note: Natural tan skin and pointed ears preserve the owned references. Review whether the body silhouette and ear-to-head proportions distinguish this family enough from humans.

caelith.review_note: Green skin with white hair is one example of independent skin/hair choices. Version 1 shortened the ears; version 2 restores the longer pointed silhouette. Skin RGB and all six hair colors remain required.

wolf.review_note: Gray/brown/cream fur and a full animal muzzle. Review the neck ruff and transition into the collar, head scale and male/female body distinction.

bear.review_note: Brown fur, round ears and a broad animal muzzle. The clothed body remains close to the common humanoid base; review whether the shoulder/torso mass is sufficient for the intended bear form.

puma.review_note: Unspotted tawny coat and a feline muzzle, using the corrected puma_head_v2 reference. Review head scale, muzzle depth and collar transition.

jaguar.review_note: Golden coat, dark rosettes and a broad feline muzzle. Review jaguar identity, head scale and whether rosettes remain readable at gameplay distance.

module_contract.requirement: Race/sex anatomy and shared animation landmarks; clothing must not be baked into the body. Covered anatomy is not validated by these images.
Separate head with a clean neck join. Four distinct faces per humanoid sex remain required; beast heads retain their animal identity.
Separate interchangeable scalp/hair modules. Four styles and six colors per humanoid sex remain required. Animal fur does not become a human hairstyle.
Independent skin/fur hands and equipment attachment. Gloves in these boards conceal fingers; exposed hands still need actual model review.
Shirt, trousers, belt, gloves and boots are separate garments with compatible attachments and coverage. These boards do not demonstrate interchangeable meshes.
Weapons, shields and armor attach independently and must fit the approved bodies. No outfit Cartesian-product meshes; no new equipment is granted by appearance.

limitations: Concept images are not 3D files or native runtime captures.
Clothing hides the underlying body, fingers and feet; no attachment, topology or animation proof is claimed.
Face/hair catalogs, palette masking, garment fitting and native performance remain unimplemented by this patch.
Each board is independently framed; apparent size differences do not define numeric height, collision or balance.
No tail or new limb configuration is proposed here; any anatomy beyond existing references remains unauthored.
Painted views are an artist brief, not geometrically identical projections from one model.
